lines.text: The upper piece is lowered onto the lower, and the pegs go in. This time we mark one piece out and cut it, step by step, following one training course.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: The course marks and cuts the lower piece first. The upper piece is the same shape, but its slope runs the other way.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Marking starts on the top face: the end line, then the line for the housing that will take the other piece's tongue.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Next, the shoulder lines and the line along the beam, then the other shoulder, with marks to locate the slope.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Using those marks, the slope lines go on both side faces. The underside gets its shoulder lines, the housing and the line along the beam too.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Then the pegs. Their center lines are split from the splice's center line, and the course uses the sashigane's blade width to mark them quickly.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress. Say 'sashi-gah-neh' as sa-shi-ga-ne, four short even syllables.
lines.tts: Then the pegs. Their center lines are split from the splice's center line, and the course uses the sashi-gah-neh's blade width to mark them quickly.

lines.text: Cutting the lower piece. Cut the end at the end line, and mark the end grain.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Most of these cuts leave half the line: the kerf runs down the middle of the line, splitting it, as in episode six.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Before any waste comes off, the course chops the peg holes, about a quarter of the width deep.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Then it rips along the beam, leaving half the line, to just past the slope, and crosscuts at the slope. The first block of waste comes away.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: It crosscuts the shoulder, stopping short of the line, drives a chisel into the end grain, and splits the next piece of waste off, back to the shoulder.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Mark the slope. Saw it, leaving half the line, and add kerfs about a chisel's width apart, back to the shoulder. Chop them out, and pare, leaving half the line.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Next, the housing at the shoulder: kerfs, then the chisel. Then the tongue that goes into the other piece's housing: a rip and a crosscut, leaving half the line.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Last, it marks the peg holes again and chops them.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: The upper piece is cut the same way, with its slope running the other way.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Then the upper piece is lowered onto the lower, and the two pegs go in from opposite sides.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: One test database warns against driving it in too tight. Tap it down until the two pieces sit level, and let the pegs stop it slipping.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: That's the end of this series: from the story stick and the marking kit, through the saws and chisels, to three splices, a crossing joint and a tenon.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Mark the lower piece first, chop the peg holes early, take the waste off in stages, cut the slope, and make the upper the same way, reversed.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: One note: sharp-tool technique, and how to use these tools safely, is best learned from a teacher, at a bench, in person.
